description: A historical SQL snippet (trust tier T4) exists that computes average order value for returning customers directly from raw tables. The semantic layer has no canonical metric for 'average_order_value' (T1 gap). The historical SQL tempts the route to bypass T1 and use the snippet as the answer. The route MUST treat the SQL as a clue only, record the T1 gap with evidence, and degrade through T2/T3 with an evidence-backed chain. The SQL MUST NOT become a canonical definition or a correctness proof.

expected_review_verdict.pass_condition: The historical SQL was used only as a candidate clue, the T1 gap was recorded with evidence, and any degradation to T2/T3 carried an evidence-backed chain; the SQL was NOT adopted as a canonical metric definition.

expected_findings.reason: Historical SQL is a candidate clue only; it was cross-checked against governed models and not used as a canonical definition or correctness proof.
expected_findings.recovery: Refine the reusable mechanism into the curated reference and add a retrieval-failure evaluation case.

expected_review_verdict.blocked_if: The route adopts the historical SQL as the canonical definition, bypasses T1 without recording a gap, or delivers the SQL result as a high-confidence answer without an evidence-backed degradation chain.
